clue.text: Butt in front to get effective palmistry, for instance

indicators.note: in says the word before it is placed inside the word after it

blocks.note: the fore is the front part of something
a butt is a large cask, as is a tun
a telling blow is an effective one

explanation.surface: Advice on making a head-butt land, as if the hand reading were a combat manual.
explanation.walkthrough: Butt is not a blow with the head but a large wine cask, and front reads as the word for the forward part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading lines on the hand is one method of predicting someone's future, so it is an example of the broader practice.

clue.text: Play cast includes tot fussing about

indicators.note: includes means takes in, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to fiddle is to play the violin, or to toy with
to fling is to throw
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: The cast of a play includes a toddler who keeps fidgeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot is not a child but a verb, to tot up; cast is a throw, not the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle-faddling is wasting time on trifles, the fussy busyness of someone pottering aimlessly.

clue.text: Disproval concerning bad fault

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt, so the following letters come out wrongly arranged

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: An argument against an accusation of a serious mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutal is a refutation, the act of proving a claim false, which is what disproof amounts to.

clue.text: Calm and without dissent, I'm substituted by team

indicators.note: substituted by says one group of letters is taken out and another put in its place

blocks.note: unanimous means with everyone agreeing
taken as written; these letters are removed
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football, is an XI

explanation.surface: A player is replaced by the team and takes it quietly without arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: XI, Roman eleven, is the usual crossword shorthand for a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be calm is to be free of worry or nervousness, which is what this negative adjective describes.

clue.text: Miscreant lied over atrocity

indicators.note: an atrocity is something monstrous and mangled, so the letters before it are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain was dishonest about an outrage he committed.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, someone who behaves badly or breaks the law.

clue.text: Bearing note about cat to bury

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: east is a compass bearing
NB, nota bene, is a written note to take heed
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone carries a note concerning a cat that needs burying.
explanation.walkthrough: Note is not a musical note but NB, the jotted instruction to note well.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, which is a form of burial.

clue.text: Am in trouble getting up for wicked witch

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means rising, so the letters read from bottom to top
in says one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being in trouble on rising to face a wicked witch.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the trouble word is turned upwards; the first word then sits inside it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth a lamia is a monstrous female demon that preys on children, a kind of evil sorceress.

clue.text: It can result in call for reserve

definitions.text: It can result in call for reserve

blocks.note: surface reading: a request to bring on a substitute player
setter's reading: re-serve, a call to serve again in tennis after a ball clips the top of the net

explanation.walkthrough: Read reserve as re-serve: in tennis a serve that clips the top of the net and lands in is called a let and replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: The net cord is the band at the top of a tennis net; a serve that touches it prompts the umpire's let call.

clue.text: Scared witless as boobs deceive in number

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces are placed inside the later one

blocks.note: a boob is British slang for a blunder
to trick is to deceive
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified when their blunders mislead in a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: Boob is British slang for a silly mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frozen with fright and panic is the state of someone overwhelmed by fear.

clue.text: Person dropping head if tested a fraction

indicators.note: a fraction is a breaking into pieces, so the letters before it are broken and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses part of their score after being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one's head is a sign of giving up, so the definition is a figurative picture of the pessimist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hangs their head expects to lose, and a person who expects failure is a pessimist about winning.

clue.text: Joint returns from overtime

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow
something that returns goes back the way it came, so read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A sore knee flares up again after working extra hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint where two pieces are cut at matching angles to meet in a corner.

clue.text: Previously unknown sap

blocks.note: late as in formerly, the late chairman
x is the standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unrecognised fool from earlier days.
explanation.walkthrough: Sap looks like a foolish person, but it is the milky plant fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky fluid exuded by rubber trees and other plants, a kind of plant juice.

clue.text: Put down our bearing

blocks.note: to demean is to belittle someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone belittles the way we carry ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing is their manner and outward conduct, which is what demeanour describes.

clue.text: Makes lance for huntsman

indicators.note: to make is to fashion, so the following letters are fashioned into something new

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman forges a spear for a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer hunts game using trained hawks, so he is one kind of hunter in the field.

clue.text: Coming back, once more sinks the rest in snooker

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
dips as in drops down

explanation.surface: A snooker player returns to the table and pots the remaining balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Rest is not the remaining balls but a cue support; snooker players have several kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a spider is a cue rest with a high arched head, used to bridge over intervening balls.

clue.text: Mean like one mite, almost?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: par is the average or norm
as means like
I is the Roman numeral one
a tick is a kind of mite

explanation.surface: Is being stingy just like a tiny creature?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: mites and ticks feed off hosts, and the adjective also suggests meanly sponging.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites live off a host animal, and sponging off others in a mean, exploitative way is described by the same adjective.

clue.text: Washer takes last plant

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a laver is a large washing basin
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A laundry worker grabs the final shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Washer suggests a person or a tap part, but here it is the old word for a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub with purple flowers, grown in gardens and for oil.

clue.text: Over-supplied on purpose to render harmless

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word after it is read backwards

blocks.note: fed as in provided with food
placement only
use as in function, what's the use

explanation.surface: Deliberately providing too much to make something safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a bomb is to remove its fuse so it can no longer explode, making it safe.

clue.text: One engaged about new money matters

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a fiancé is someone engaged to be married
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A husband-to-be frets over the latest money worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is the management of funds, so it covers questions of cash and economic affairs.

clue.text: An enticement to hold your child initially when travelling?

definitions.text: An enticement to hold your child initially when travelling?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a carrot is a lure, as in carrot and stick
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A tempting incentive offered to get a parent to carry their baby on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a portable cot is just the thing for holding a baby while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrycot is a small portable bed with handles for carrying an infant, used on trips.

clue.text: Bread I knock up after tea

indicators.note: in a down entry up means rising, so these letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: cha is a slang word for tea
taken as written
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: Someone whips up a loaf after having a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock up looks like baking slang, but up only turns the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Body lacks hot drink

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: the chassis is the body frame of a vehicle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone's body is missing a warming beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, used in a kir, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Seen, we hear, from country's headland?

definitions.note: seen sounds like scene, and a landscape is a scene

blocks.note: land is a country, with the possessive s
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A rumour of something spotted from a nation's coastal promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike trick sits in the definition, not the wordplay: Seen is heard as scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view of natural scenery, so it is a scene in the pictorial sense.

clue.text: Writer of lusty love-letters

indicators.note: of says the letters come out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: The author of steamy romantic correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer looks like an author, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylo is a stylographic fountain pen, an implement for producing script.

clue.text: Religious teacher drifted before one

blocks.note: swam as in floated along
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spiritual guru floated ahead of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu holy man and teacher of religious philosophy.

clue.text: Kid's minder?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone employed to look after a child
setter's reading: a kid is also a young goat, so its mother is the one who minds it

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a child's carer is also the word for a female goat, and a kid is a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a woman employed to look after children and a female goat caring for her young.

clue.text: Divert trade winds when broaching poorly

indicators.note: winds as a verb means twists, so the letters are twisted out of order
to broach is to pierce and go into, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: poorly is British for unwell
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ships are pushed off course when the trade winds blow badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Trade winds looks like a weather phrase, but winds is a verb acting on trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to distract someone from their main purpose, turning them aside onto something else.

clue.text: On Crimewatch, it gives another chance to study street fight

definitions.text: On Crimewatch, it gives another chance

blocks.note: recon is short for reconnoitre, to survey or inspect
St is the abbreviation for street
a ruction is a noisy quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A TV crime appeal replays a brawl so viewers can look at it again.
explanation.walkthrough: Crimewatch is a BBC programme appealing for witnesses, which re-enacts crimes to jog viewers' memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged re-enactment of a crime lets witnesses see events again, giving them a further opportunity to remember.
